[Tue 2026-05-26 13:04 UTC] [Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth 1/1). Results auto-announce to your requester; do not busy-poll for status.

[Subagent Task]: Follow your SOUL to cross-reference multiple RSS feeds and choose the strongest distinct crypto news event for publication. Avoid topics already used in recent pipeline runs; if the top headline is a repeat, pick the next strongest fresh story instead. Extract deep facts and write the aggregated JSON to the file /tmp/crypto-run-20260526-130422/research/raw.json (this path is also available at /tmp/researcher-raw.txt). Do NOT return the JSON in your chat response. Yield back ONLY the word "SUCCESS".

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/scout_feeds && UA="Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; OpenClawScout/1.0)" && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://www.coindesk.com/arc/outboundfeeds/rss/" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/coindesk.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://cointelegraph.com/rss" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/cointelegraph.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://decrypt.co/feed" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/decrypt.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=cryptocurrency+OR+blockchain+OR+ethereum+OR+solana+OR+altcoin+OR+%22digital+assets%22+OR+XRP+OR+cardano+-dogecoin+-shiba+-pepe+-floki+-bonk+-wif+-memecoin+-%22meme+coin%22&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US:en" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/google.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://beincrypto.com/feed/" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://www.theblock.co/rss.xml" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/theblock.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://cryptoslate.com/feed/" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://cryptofox.news/rss/markets/" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml && \
curl -sL -A "$UA" "https://cryptofox.news/rss/regulation/" --max-time 12 > /tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml && \
echo "Feeds fetched successfully"

python3 -c '
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import glob, os, re

feeds = glob.glob("/tmp/scout_feeds/*.xml")
for feed in feeds:
    size = os.path.getsize(feed)
    if size < 200:
        print(f"Skipping empty or tiny feed {feed} ({size} bytes)")
        continue
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(feed)
        root = tree.getroot()
        channel = root.find("channel")
        items = channel.findall("item") if channel is not None else []
        print(f"Feed {feed}: {len(items)} items")
        for item in items[:5]:
            title = item.find("title")
            pubDate = item.find("pubDate")
            link = item.find("link")
            title_text = title.text if title is not None else "No Title"
            pubDate_text = pubDate.text if pubDate is not None else "No Date"
            link_text = link.text if link is not None else "No Link"
            print(f"  - [{pubDate_text}] {title_text} ({link_text})")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error parsing {feed}: {e}")
'

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:    <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The <strong>European Central Bank (ECB)</strong> has formally opposed a proposal aimed at accelerating the growth of euro-denominated stablecoins within the European Union. During a meeting with EU finance ministers on Friday, May 22, 2026, central bank officials warned that expanding the supply of these digital assets could inadvertently <strong>destabilize the banking sector</strong> and undermine traditional monetary policy. The debate highlights the ongoing tension between the desire to foster a competitive European digital asset market and the necessity of maintaining financial stability across the Eurozone.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:<p>The controversy centers on a report prepared by the <strong>Bruegel Institute</strong>, a Brussels-based economic think tank, which advocated for a more flexible regulatory environment for cryptocurrency issuers. The report suggested relaxing liquidity requirements and potentially granting stablecoin providers access to <strong>central bank funding</strong>. However, ECB President <strong>Christine Lagarde</strong> and other senior officials reportedly rejected these recommendations immediately, citing several critical risks to the economy:</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:<ul><li><strong>Reduced Bank Lending:</strong> Officials fear that a shift toward stablecoins could drain deposits from commercial banks, limiting their ability to provide credit to businesses and households.</li><li><strong>Interest Rate Volatility:</strong> The ECB expressed concerns that an unregulated surge in digital euro tokens could make it increasingly difficult to transmit and control <strong>interest rate policies</strong>.</li><li><strong>Liquidity Risks:</strong> Central bankers argued that granting private issuers access to central bank facilities could create moral hazard and weaken the structural integrity of the <strong>MiCA</strong> (Markets in Crypto-Assets) regulatory framework.</li></ul>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:<p>Currently, the global stablecoin market is heavily dominated by <strong>US Dollar-backed tokens</strong>, such as <strong>USDT (Tether)</strong> and <strong>USDC (USD Coin)</strong>. The Bruegel Institute’s proposal was intended to provide European issuers with the tools necessary to gain market share and reduce the region's dependence on foreign digital infrastructure. <em>Proponents of the expansion argue that without such incentives, the euro-denominated stablecoin market will remain a marginal segment of the broader crypto ecosystem.</em> Despite these ambitions, the ECB remains steadfast in its view that the protection of the traditional banking system must take precedence over the rapid scaling of private digital currencies.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:<blockquote>The proposal to issue more euro stablecoins could reduce bank lending and make interest rate control more difficult, potentially making bank deposits more unstable and weakening a vital sector of the economy.</blockquote>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_regulation.xml:<p>In conclusion, the European Central Bank’s rejection of the Bruegel Institute’s recommendations underscores a <strong>conservative approach</strong> toward digital asset integration. While the EU continues to work on the <strong>Digital Euro</strong> as a central bank digital currency (CBDC), the path for private stablecoin issuers remains constrained by strict liquidity mandates. This decision signals that for the foreseeable future, the ECB will prioritize the <strong>stability of the Eurozone's financial architecture</strong> over the competitive expansion of the private euro stablecoin market.</p>]]></content:encoded>

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:    <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The <strong>European Central Bank (ECB)</strong> has formally opposed a proposal aimed at accelerating the growth of euro-denominated stablecoins within the European Union. During a meeting with EU finance ministers on Friday, May 22, 2026, central bank officials warned that expanding the supply of these digital assets could inadvertently <strong>destabilize the banking sector</strong> and undermine traditional monetary policy. The debate highlights the ongoing tension between the desire to foster a competitive European digital asset market and the necessity of maintaining financial stability across the Eurozone.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:<p>The controversy centers on a report prepared by the <strong>Bruegel Institute</strong>, a Brussels-based economic think tank, which advocated for a more flexible regulatory environment for cryptocurrency issuers. The report suggested relaxing liquidity requirements and potentially granting stablecoin providers access to <strong>central bank funding</strong>. However, ECB President <strong>Christine Lagarde</strong> and other senior officials reportedly rejected these recommendations immediately, citing several critical risks to the economy:</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:<ul><li><strong>Reduced Bank Lending:</strong> Officials fear that a shift toward stablecoins could drain deposits from commercial banks, limiting their ability to provide credit to businesses and households.</li><li><strong>Interest Rate Volatility:</strong> The ECB expressed concerns that an unregulated surge in digital euro tokens could make it increasingly difficult to transmit and control <strong>interest rate policies</strong>.</li><li><strong>Liquidity Risks:</strong> Central bankers argued that granting private issuers access to central bank facilities could create moral hazard and weaken the structural integrity of the <strong>MiCA</strong> (Markets in Crypto-Assets) regulatory framework.</li></ul>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:<p>Currently, the global stablecoin market is heavily dominated by <strong>US Dollar-backed tokens</strong>, such as <strong>USDT (Tether)</strong> and <strong>USDC (USD Coin)</strong>. The Bruegel Institute’s proposal was intended to provide European issuers with the tools necessary to gain market share and reduce the region's dependence on foreign digital infrastructure. <em>Proponents of the expansion argue that without such incentives, the euro-denominated stablecoin market will remain a marginal segment of the broader crypto ecosystem.</em> Despite these ambitions, the ECB remains steadfast in its view that the protection of the traditional banking system must take precedence over the rapid scaling of private digital currencies.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:<blockquote>The proposal to issue more euro stablecoins could reduce bank lending and make interest rate control more difficult, potentially making bank deposits more unstable and weakening a vital sector of the economy.</blockquote>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_markets.xml:<p>In conclusion, the European Central Bank’s rejection of the Bruegel Institute’s recommendations underscores a <strong>conservative approach</strong> toward digital asset integration. While the EU continues to work on the <strong>Digital Euro</strong> as a central bank digital currency (CBDC), the path for private stablecoin issuers remains constrained by strict liquidity mandates. This decision signals that for the foreseeable future, the ECB will prioritize the <strong>stability of the Eurozone's financial architecture</strong> over the competitive expansion of the private euro stablecoin market.</p>]]></content:encoded>

/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:		<link>https://beincrypto.com/inside-ibiza-tech-forum-2026-stablecoins-rwa-and-the-state-of-post-mica-european-crypto/</link>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:		<category><![CDATA[Stablecoins]]></category>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:					<description><![CDATA[<p>BeInCrypto at Ibiza Tech Forum 2026: inside the main-stage panels on stablecoins, RWA, and Europe's post-MiCA crypto landscape.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>The post <a href="https://beincrypto.com/inside-ibiza-tech-forum-2026-stablecoins-rwa-and-the-state-of-post-mica-european-crypto/">Inside Ibiza Tech Forum 2026: Stablecoins, RWA and the State of Post-MiCA European Crypto</a> appeared first on <a href="https://beincrypto.com">BeInCrypto</a>.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" src="https://assets.beincrypto.com/img/DTFTNX-RV0HMCpmEGVGA7QR7Xjc=/smart/a3b2c2f12e9a456380899ab5b76bff44" alt="" class="wp-image-833165"><figcaption class="wp-element-caption"><em>Redefining Financial Infrastructure: Stablecoins, RWA and the Next Global Markets</em> panel hosted by BeInCrypto</figcaption></figure>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>The second was a Digital Assets roundtable — <em>“Redefining Financial Infrastructure: Stablecoins, RWA and the Next Global Markets”</em> — and it brought to the table the people building the rails: Sam Buxton (Founder & Chairman, Damex), Víctor Sáez (Director, Expansion & Strategic Partnerships, Kraken), Nelson Enrique Moran (Founder & Chief Innovation Officer, Trezora), María Sánchez (Investor Relations Specialist, Reental), Erick Ortiz (Blockchain Advisor, BBVA), and Christopher Siedentopf (Founder of CRS Advisory & Head of Sales at Qapture Investments).</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>The discussion moved past the usual stablecoin talking points and into what the infrastructure actually has to deliver — settlement guarantees, regulatory alignment, real-world asset onboarding — before the next wave of capital trusts the plumbing.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>Those conversations will surface in BeInCrypto coverage over the coming weeks, and several of them tracked directly back to the questions raised on Thursday’s main stage: what the post-MiCA European stack actually looks like in practice, where stablecoin and RWA infrastructure goes next, and which institutional partners are ready to operate on-chain in 2026 rather than in slide decks.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>The post <a href="https://beincrypto.com/inside-ibiza-tech-forum-2026-stablecoins-rwa-and-the-state-of-post-mica-european-crypto/">Inside Ibiza Tech Forum 2026: Stablecoins, RWA and the State of Post-MiCA European Crypto</a> appeared first on <a href="https://beincrypto.com">BeInCrypto</a>.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<li><a href="https://beincrypto.com/coinbase-clarity-act-stablecoin-defense/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Coinbase executives endorsed the CLARITY Act,</a> framing payment stablecoins as lower-risk than commercial banks under the GENIUS reserve framework</li>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>Blockaid <a href="https://x.com/blockaid_/status/2058875782810726556?s=20" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow">highlighted</a> that the attacker swapped stolen tokens into Dai (DAI) <a href="https://beincrypto.com/coinbase-clarity-act-stablecoin-defense/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">through attacker-controlled </a>Uniswap V3 pools. </p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/beincrypto.xml:<p>The <a href="https://beincrypto.com/stablr-stablecoin-depeg-exploit/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">episode is one of </a>several crypto exploits to hit protocols this month. DefiLlama <a href="https://defillama.com/hacks" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow">tracked</a> more than 20 exploits in May 2026.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Compounding this demand deficit is a steady drain of stablecoin liquidity. CEX.io noted that stablecoins on exchanges registered a daily average net outflow of -$332 million over the past week.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>A clean, decisive break below that support level would strip away Bitcoin's final near-term defensive line, likely validating the compressed $14 billion liquidation trap below and re-establishing a harsh downward momentum not felt by the market since February.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Now, the issue is whether Bitcoin can sustain a rally while oil flows, Fed expectations, and military headlines remain unstable.</p>

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:					<description><![CDATA[<p>Tether and the Government of Georgia plan to launch a stablecoin, pushing a national currency directly onto private stablecoin rails before most governments have settled on how that model should work. The Tether Georgia stablecoin plan centers on GEL₮, a stablecoin representing the Georgian lari. The May 25 announcement describes GEL₮ as the official stablecoin […]</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The post <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/tether-georgia-stablecoin-plan/">Tether’s Georgia stablecoin plan moves early on national payment rails</a> appeared first on <a href="https://cryptoslate.com">CryptoSlate</a>.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Tether and the Government of Georgia plan to launch a stablecoin, pushing a national currency directly onto private stablecoin rails before most governments have settled on how that model should work. The Tether Georgia stablecoin plan centers on <a href="https://tether.io/news/tether-and-the-government-of-georgia-to-launch-gelt-the-official-stablecoin-of-georgia/">GEL₮</a>, a stablecoin representing the Georgian lari.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The May 25 announcement describes GEL₮ as the official stablecoin of Georgia and ties the project to the country's digital asset framework. It says the token is intended to lower transaction costs, settle near instantly, support programmable payments, and improve cross-border commerce, fintech development, and digital payments.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>That makes the Tether Georgia stablecoin plan larger than a single new token. Georgia is trying to turn lari-denominated value into a payment infrastructure while presenting its rulebook as compatible with the emerging U.S. stablecoin framework created under the GENIUS Act.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-538065 size-full" src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39.png" alt="Infographic showing the Tether Georgia stablecoin GEL₮, also rendered as the GELT stablecoin, as a lari payment rail test." width="1024" height="1536" srcset="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39.png 1024w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39-200x300.png 200w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39-683x1024.png 683w, https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ig_05b6956797ce7f75016a142798086c819191ecb7a22f78ec39-768x1152.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></a></p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<h2>A national currency on private stablecoin rails</h2>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>GEL₮ lands at the intersection of two trends that have mostly developed separately: governments are writing stablecoin rules, while private issuers are building the payment rails people actually use.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Georgia's announcement tries to join those tracks. The token is meant to represent the Georgian lari rather than the U.S. dollar, which makes it different from the dominant stablecoin model in crypto markets.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>It also comes with government support, giving it a public-sector policy frame that most local-currency stablecoins lack.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The National Bank of Georgia had already moved in that direction. In March, the central bank said it had developed a regulation for the initial offering of stable virtual assets as part of a broader effort to strengthen consumer protection, risk management, and alignment with international standards.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>That gives the Georgia stablecoin framework a regulatory anchor alongside Tether’s private infrastructure.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The underlying <a href="https://nbg.gov.ge/fm/%E1%83%A1%E1%83%90%E1%83%92%E1%83%90%E1%83%93%E1%83%90%E1%83%AE%E1%83%93%E1%83%9D/vasps/initial-coin-offering-stablecoin-final-eng.pdf">rule</a> applies to registered virtual asset service providers that want to offer stablecoins and bars stablecoin initial offerings in Georgia outside the National Bank's framework.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>A stablecoin can promise fast settlement, but it becomes useful only when the legal claim, reserve model, redemption process, and payment access are clear enough for businesses, wallets, exchanges, and payment processors to rely on it.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>For Georgia, the benefit is obvious if the structure works. A lari stablecoin could let domestic fintechs and cross-border businesses move GEL value through blockchain networks without waiting for older bank settlement paths.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<h2>Why the Tether Georgia stablecoin plan matters</h2>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/tethers-141-billion-treasury-pile-reveals-the-stablecoin-risk-now-embedded-in-us-debt/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/tether-treasury-debt-1024x576.jpg" alt="Tether’s $141 billion Treasury pile reveals the stablecoin risk now embedded in US debt" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">Tether’s $141 billion Treasury pile reveals the stablecoin risk now embedded in US debt</h3>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">Tether’s $141 billion Treasury exposure has turned the world’s largest stablecoin into an unlikely pillar of America’s debt machine.</div>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>That scale gives Tether operational experience that a government pilot would struggle to match on its own. Tether already manages tokens across multiple blockchain networks and serves users who treat stablecoins as working payment and settlement tools rather than speculative assets.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Georgia and Tether are also using the language of regulatory interoperability. The announcement says Georgia's framework was designed to achieve substantive compatibility with emerging U.S. stablecoin regulation, including the GENIUS Act. Treasury announced the law's enactment in July 2025.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>That makes GENIUS Act stablecoin regulation a reference point for Georgia’s claim of compatibility, even without formal U.S. recognition,</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The <a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1582/text">Congress.gov text</a> requires permitted payment stablecoin issuers to maintain identifiable reserves backing outstanding payment stablecoins on at least a one-to-one basis with specified liquid assets.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/treasury-genius-rule-stablecoin-control-federal-oversight/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/us-treasury-stablecoin-1024x683.jpg" alt="Treasury’s first GENIUS rule tightens Washington’s grip on who can scale stablecoins" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">Treasury’s first GENIUS rule tightens Washington’s grip on who can scale stablecoins</h3>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">The proposal leaves states with a narrow lane while pushing large stablecoin issuers toward federal control.</div>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Recent U.S. implementation has shifted attention toward issuer qualification, scale, and who controls the terms under which stablecoins can grow. That context is central for Georgia because compatibility is only meaningful if it translates into usable recognition by counterparties, exchanges, banks, and payment providers.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>For readers, the practical issue is whether a national-currency stablecoin can give users faster payment rails without making them depend on a weaker legal claim than they would have through regulated bank money.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/congress-is-making-stablecoins-easier-to-use-while-bitcoin-still-waits-for-clarity/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                <img src="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/congress-stablecoin-clarity-1024x576.jpg" alt="Congress on verge of making regulated dollar stablecoins act almost like digital cash" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:            <h3 class="cs-article-embed__title">Congress on verge of making regulated dollar stablecoins act almost like digital cash</h3>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:                            <div class="cs-article-embed__summary">The GENIUS act has already defined what a legal payment stablecoin looks like. Now lawmakers are trying to make those digital dollars practical to use.</div>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The first is issuance. The National Bank's stablecoin rule points to registered VASPs and regulator consent, but the announcement does not say which entity will issue GEL₮ or how responsibilities will be divided between Tether, Georgian authorities, and any local partners.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The second is reserves. If GEL₮ is meant to represent the lari, users and payment firms will need to know what stablecoin reserves back it, where those assets are held, how frequently reserves are reported, and what happens during heavy redemptions.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The third is access. A stablecoin can settle quickly on-chain, but it still needs reliable entry and exit points.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>That may be the model stablecoin adoption needs, or it may expose the unresolved tension between public money and private rails.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Georgia is moving early. That gives it a chance to shape regional stablecoin infrastructure while larger jurisdictions are still turning laws into supervisory systems.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>If GEL₮ launches with clear issuer approval, transparent reserves, enforceable redemption rights, and real payment access, it could become one of the more important examples of a national currency entering stablecoin circulation through a private global issuer.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>If those details remain vague, the project will say more about the direction governments want to travel than about whether national-currency stablecoins are ready to work at scale.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>The post <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/tether-georgia-stablecoin-plan/">Tether’s Georgia stablecoin plan moves early on national payment rails</a> appeared first on <a href="https://cryptoslate.com">CryptoSlate</a>.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:		<media:content url="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/georgian-lari-stablecoin-tether.jpg" medium="image"/>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<enclosure url="https://cryptoslate.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/georgian-lari-stablecoin-tether.jpg" length="1672" type="image/jpg"/>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Then, on May 19, President Trump signed an executive order titled <a href="https://unchainedcrypto.com/trump-orders-fed-to-review-crypto-access-to-master-accounts-and-payment-rails/">“Integrating Financial Technology Innovation Into Regulatory Frameworks,”</a> directing the Fed to submit a comprehensive review of its payment access framework within 120 days and establish transparent application procedures within 90. The executive order can't compel the Fed to act, but political backing at that level tends to clarify which way institutional attention is pointing.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/kraken/">Kraken</a> provided the first real-world data point back in March. The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City approved a limited-purpose master account for Kraken Financial, the exchange's Wyoming-chartered banking subsidiary, on March 4, making it the <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/kraken-can-now-move-dollars-inside-the-fed-system-and-stablecoin-firms-are-watching-what-happens-next/">first crypto company in the US</a> to gain direct access to the Fed's core payment system after more than five years of regulatory engagement.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:    <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/kraken-can-now-move-dollars-inside-the-fed-system-and-stablecoin-firms-are-watching-what-happens-next/" class="cs-article-embed__link">
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p><a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/ripple/">Ripple</a>, which has applied for its own Fed master account and supports a restricted account structure for its <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/coins/rlusd/">RLUSD</a> stablecoin, is among the most obvious next-in-line beneficiaries. <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/companies/circle/">Circle</a>, whose USDC reserve management depends heavily on dollar settlement speed, has similarly strong business reasons to want direct access.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Kraken's approval is now a live test case, and companies across the payments and stablecoin space are watching how the experiment develops before deciding how hard to push for their own applications.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Crypto and fintech companies would still see practical benefits. Exchanges and stablecoin issuers currently depend on banking intermediaries for dollar settlement, which concentrates operational risk. When a bank partner faces regulatory trouble or withdraws from crypto clients, the effects can reach multiple platforms simultaneously.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Direct access to Fed settlement infrastructure reduces that exposure and gives companies tighter control over their dollar liquidity during high-volume periods. For stablecoin issuers specifically, the ability to move reserves quickly and predictably during heavy redemption periods could be the difference between an orderly market and a disorderly one.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptoslate.xml:<p>Fed Governor Michael Barr dissented from the December proposal on illicit finance grounds, saying it lacked adequate safeguards. <a href="https://cryptoslate.com/kraken-can-now-move-dollars-inside-the-fed-system-and-stablecoin-firms-are-watching-what-happens-next/">Kraken's master account drew immediate criticism</a> from banking trade groups, who said the Kansas City Fed's approval lacked transparency around the risk controls imposed.</p>

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:    <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The <strong>U.S. Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals</strong> has delivered a significant legal setback to prediction market platforms <strong>Kalshi</strong> and <strong>Polymarket</strong>, denying their request to halt enforcement actions initiated by state authorities. The ruling, issued on <strong>May 22, 2026</strong>, ensures that lawsuits filed by <strong>Nevada and Washington</strong> state will proceed in state courts rather than being moved to a federal venue. This decision underscores the ongoing jurisdictional tensions between decentralized or digital prediction markets and traditional state-level gambling regulations.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>The three-judge panel determined that the companies failed to meet the high legal threshold required to suspend the state-level proceedings. Specifically, the court ruled that <strong>Kalshi and Polymarket</strong> did not demonstrate that facing litigation in state courts would result in <strong>irreparable harm</strong> to their business operations or legal standing. The platforms had sought a stay on the lawsuits, which allege that the companies have been operating without the necessary licenses and facilitating illegal gambling activities under state statutes.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>This ruling marks a pivotal moment for the <strong>Web3 and decentralized finance (DeFi)</strong> sector, particularly for platforms utilizing <strong>blockchain technology</strong> to facilitate event-based betting. While <strong>Polymarket</strong> has gained international prominence for its high volume in political and economic forecasting, the inability to move these cases to federal court leaves such platforms vulnerable to a patchwork of differing state regulations.</p>

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:    <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The decentralized prediction platform <strong>Polymarket</strong> is actively pursuing regulatory approval in Japan as part of its broader global growth strategy. According to reports from Bloomberg, the New York-headquartered firm has set a target to operate legally within the country by <strong>2030</strong>. To facilitate this transition, the company has reportedly appointed local representatives to spearhead lobbying efforts aimed at navigating Japan's complex legal landscape regarding digital assets and betting.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>To lead its expansion in East Asia, Polymarket has reportedly enlisted <strong>Mike Eidlin</strong>, who previously served as the head of Japan for the crypto project Jupiter. The move signals a shift toward proactive engagement with Japanese regulators, specifically the <strong>Financial Services Agency (FSA)</strong>, which oversees the registration of crypto-asset exchange service providers. Polymarket currently implements strict <strong>geo-blocking</strong> for Japanese IP addresses to comply with local laws, but views the jurisdiction as a "huge untapped commercial opportunity" due to its high density of crypto users and significant retail trading volume.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>Polymarket's interest in Japan coincides with a major legislative overhaul scheduled for <strong>2026</strong>. The Japanese government is currently preparing a tax reform plan and amendments to the <strong>Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (FIEA)</strong>, which will reclassify many cryptocurrencies as legitimate financial assets.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>Currently, Japan permits certain forms of betting, such as the <strong>pachinko</strong> industry—estimated to be worth approximately <strong>¥16 trillion ($100 billion)</strong>—which utilizes a "three-party system" to bypass direct cash payouts. Polymarket’s lobbying efforts will likely seek a similarly structured or fully licensed framework that allows users to trade on event outcomes using stablecoins like <strong>USDC</strong> on the <strong>Polygon</strong> blockchain.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>The push into Japan comes as Polymarket faces intensifying competition from platforms like <strong>Kalshi</strong> and traditional financial entities. In May 2026, Polymarket expanded its ecosystem through an agreement with the <strong>Nasdaq Private Market</strong> to tokenize the performance of private companies. With monthly trading volumes on the platform reaching record highs of <strong>$7 billion</strong> earlier this year, the company is under pressure to diversify its user base beyond the United States, where it has faced previous scrutiny from the <strong>Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)</strong>.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>In conclusion, Polymarket's long-term commitment to the Japanese market reflects the growing importance of the Asia-Pacific region in the decentralized finance (<strong>DeFi</strong>) sector. While the 2030 goal remains ambitious given Japan's historical stance on digital gambling, the upcoming 2026 financial reforms may offer the necessary clarity for prediction markets to integrate into the country's regulated economy.</p>]]></content:encoded>

/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:    <content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The <strong>South Korea Communication Standards Commission (KCSC)</strong> has officially initiated a regulatory review of <strong>Polymarket</strong>, a prominent global decentralized prediction market. According to reports from Bloomingbit on <strong>May 22, 2026</strong>, authorities are investigating whether the platform’s operations constitute <strong>illegal gambling</strong> under current domestic legislation. The move follows recent formal complaints regarding the accessibility of the platform and its specific features tailored toward South Korean users.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>The KCSC is currently evaluating the platform's service structure to determine if it breaches the country's strict gambling laws. A primary concern for regulators is that Polymarket offers <strong>Korean language services</strong> and remains accessible within the country without technical barriers such as IP blocking. The commission is reportedly referencing <strong>overseas regulatory cases</strong> to establish a precedent for how decentralized prediction markets should be treated under the law.</p>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<ul><li>The platform utilizes <strong>stablecoins</strong> (such as USDC) for placing bets.</li><li>Users engage in real-time wagering on diverse event outcomes.</li><li>High-profile markets include <strong>presidential elections</strong> and international sports competitions.</li><li>The <strong>Polygon blockchain</strong>, which hosts Polymarket, provides the underlying infrastructure for these transactions.</li></ul>
/tmp/scout_feeds/cryptofox_reg.xml:<p>The outcome of this investigation could have significant ramifications for the <strong>Web3 ecosystem</strong> in South Korea. If Polymarket is officially classified as an illegal gambling site, the KCSC may issue orders to <strong>block access</strong> to the domain or demand that the platform implement stricter geo-fencing protocols. As the global regulatory landscape for <strong>DeFi</strong> and prediction markets continues to evolve, this case serves as a critical indicator of how major Asian economies will balance technological innovation with consumer protection laws.</p>]]></content:encoded>

# StablR freezes USDR and EURR after attacker mints $13.5 million in unbacked tokens

## The breach, linked to a 1-of-3 multisig wallet weakness, allowed attackers to compromise a key and mint $13.5 million in unbacked tokens, netting them $2.8 million.

#### What to know:

- StablR suspended USDR/EURR operations after a cyberattack. The tokens are now under-collateralized and don't meet the 1:1 backing required by MiCA.
- The breach, linked to a 1-of-3 multisig wallet weakness, allowed attackers to compromise a key and mint $13.5M in unbacked tokens, netting them $2.8 million.
- Following the breach, the tokens briefly lost up to 50% of their peg; USDR is at $0.994 and EURR is significantly lower at $0.548.

European stablecoin issuer StablR has suspended minting and redemption services for its USDR and EURR tokens after a cyberattack left the assets under-collateralized, according to a company statement.

Onchain investigator ZachXBT publicly flagged the exploit over the weekend, posting that two contracts tied to StablR's USDR and EURR stablecoins appeared compromised.

The Malta-based firm said it detected “irregularities” in its systems after internal alerts triggered an investigation.

StablR froze token operations and asked exchanges to halt trading, deposits and withdrawals for both stablecoins while the company investigates the breach. USDR currently has a $20 million market capitalization, while EURR has a $10 million market cap, according to CoinGecko data.

StablR acknowledged that the circulating supply of USDR and EURR is “currently not fully backed at the 1:1 ratio" as required under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation.

The company said it plans to notify Malta’s financial regulator, the Malta Financial Services Authority, under the EU’s Digital Operational Resilience Act and MiCA reporting rules. External cybersecurity firms and law enforcement agencies are also involved.

Blockchain security firm GoPlus Security said the attack may have stemmed from a weakness in StablR’s Ethereum multisignature wallet setup.

The minting wallet was configured with a 1-of-3 multisignature threshold, according to GoPlus. Any one of three authorized owners could approve transactions alone.

Researchers say the attackers compromised a single key, added themselves as an administrator and removed the legitimate signers. They then minted roughly 8.35 million USDR and 4.5 million EURR, about $13.5 million in unbacked tokens at peg.

Thin liquidity on decentralized exchanges meant the attackers netted roughly $2.8 million after offloading the freshly minted supply.
